goal: Bulk-verify cataloged Network::*Receiver vtable[1] (offset 0x4) is the alleged Receive/factory method. Sanity check Pattern A receiver catalog from the receiver-discovery pass.
method: For each of 42 distinct receiver class names from xivl-opcodes/data/client_receivers.json (43 entries; UserDataReceiver has 2 vtables), queried Ghidra vftable+0x4 via DumpVtableSlots.java (2 batches: 25+17). Also ran FindSymbolByName.java with substring "Receiver::vftable" to enumerate ALL Pattern A receiver vftables present in the binary (Application::Lua::Script::Client::Command::*::Receiver namespace).
addressing_convention_note: Ghidra vftable VA shown is absolute (image base 0x00400000 applied). client_receivers.json rtti_rva is image-base-stripped (e.g. 0xc574b0 in catalog = absolute 0x010574b0 in Ghidra). slot1_fn FUN_NAMES like FUN_0089f530 are absolute VAs (already include +0x400000).

pattern_semantics.2_slot: vtable[0]=destructor, vtable[1]=Receive entry. Verifying vtable[1] DIRECTLY validates the cataloged Receive method.
pattern_semantics.5_slot: vtable[0]=destructor, vtable[1]=New() factory, vtable[2]=Receive, vtable[3]=aux dispatch, vtable[4]=predicate. Per kick_receiver doc. vtable[1] verification proves the FACTORY, not the Receive entry; client_receivers.json slot1_fn for 5/6-slot is the factory.
pattern_semantics.6_slot: similar to 5-slot, factory at vtable[1]. UserDataReceiver and JobQuestCompleteTripleReceiver.
pattern_semantics.inventory_doc_note: slot 1 for 2-slot variants; slot 2 for 5/6-slot variants; slot 0 is the destructor. The catalog field "slot1_fn" therefore stores the factory function for 5/6-slot, and the Receive entry for 2-slot.

receiver_classes_cataloged.note_duplicate: UserDataReceiver has 2 vtable entries (primary 0xc57488 6-slot + sibling 0xc574a4 2-slot, same slot1_fn FUN_008a2a20) -> 42 unique class names, 43 catalog entries
